name: MAIN STREET, DAWN
note: EXTRACTED by tools/extract-examine.mjs from the documents its sources name -- errata 67's merge, in doc 05's, the batch's, then the repeats' order, less errata 68 H's drops. Do not edit: change the documents and re-run.

subjects.name: THE FALSE FRONTS
LOOK_AT: The same two-story faces on the same one-story buildings — but at dawn, with the light behind them, they look like what they always were: a promise somebody kept badly and everybody kept anyway.
Two stories tall in front and one story deep. It is still a stage set. It is just that people live here.
A man is painting one of them. Not the front: the back, where nobody will see it.
LISTEN_TO: Wind behind them, same as ever. It sounds less empty than it did. That may be me.
Wind. There is still a great deal of nothing behind these. It has stopped being funny and started being a fact about somebody's home.
Somebody behind one of them, frying something. The fronts finally have something behind them worth the name.

subjects.name: THE IMPROVEMENT COMPANY SIGN
LOOK_AT: The gilt is peeling off the lettering in the morning sun. Nobody will repaint it now, and the sign has the good grace to know it.
The C in COMPANY has already gone. It reads IMPROVEMENT OMPANY, which is more accurate than it used to be.
Nobody is standing under it. For twelve years somebody was always standing under it, waiting to be let in.
LISTEN_TO: It creaks. It would like to be taken down. I know another sign that felt that way.
The creak again. It has said its piece and keeps on saying it.
The chain ticking against the bracket. It will come down in its own time.

subjects.name: THE WATER TROUGH
LOOK_AT: Three inches of water, and this morning, the whole sky in it.
Somebody has cleaned it. It is still three inches of water, and it is clean water.
I can see my own face in it, and the sky behind, and neither of us looks worried.
LISTEN_TO: The thing that lives in it, surfacing. We have both made it through.
A small ripple. It has decided I am not a threat.
Nothing for a moment, then a bubble. We are both still here.

subjects.name: THE BOARDWALK
LOOK_AT: Six inches above the mud, same as ever. The distinction matters less this morning. Everyone is walking in the middle of the street anyway.
Somebody has swept it. Not the street: just the boardwalk, end to end, at dawn, for no reason anyone will admit to.
I stood on the loose board on purpose. It said what it always says. I find I had missed it.
LISTEN_TO: The loose board, third from the end. Still loose. Somebody should see to that. It will outlast us all.
Boots further down, slow ones. Nobody is in a hurry this morning.
The loose board, under my own weight this time. A friendly note. A little flat.

subjects.name: POSTED NOTICES
LOOK_AT: Under all the claims and disputes, one new notice, official, sealed, correctly spelled. It has the whole board's attention.
Claims for sale, claims disputed, and a new one: CLAIM ONE, FILED, O. MOTT, WORKINGS TO COMMENCE. The lost dog notice has been taken down.
Somebody has drawn a small raccoon in the corner of the official notice. I am choosing not to know who.
LISTEN_TO: Paper in wind. This morning it sounds like applause. I am aware that is me.
Paper, in wind. Less of it.
One sheet has come loose and gone off down the street, taking its business elsewhere.

subjects.name: THE CHURCH STEEPLE
LOOK_AT: The tallest thing in Consolation, catching the first light, as is its habit and its right.
The tallest thing in Consolation, and the only building as deep as it is tall.
A bird has landed on the cross at the top. It is the only thing in town higher than the bell, and it is not making anything of it.
LISTEN_TO: The bell. In tune. Sowerby has not changed how he strikes it. Nothing changed but everything under it.
The bell again, the note settling into the hills. It took this town twelve years to sound like this.
The last of the bell, fading. Under it, nothing out of tune at all.

subjects.name: A DOG
LOOK_AT: The dog, in the early sun, in the middle of the street, on his back. He has always known something the rest of us are only learning this morning.
Bill. He is sitting with somebody now. He does not appear to have noticed a difference.
He has rolled over to warm the other side. He had the right idea all along.
LISTEN_TO: Breathing. Contented. The town's oldest solvency, undiluted.
Breathing. Contented. He remains the only solvent resident of Consolation.
A small snore. The most honest sound on Main Street, and this morning it has competition.

overrides.TALK_TO: I thanked him. For nothing in particular. For being the town's one solvent institution. He accepted on the street's behalf.

subjects.name: THE MUD
LOOK_AT: The same mud. It held my boot the first night and the truth the whole time. The only honest thing in the territory, as I believe I remarked.
The same mud. I know it now.
My boot print from the first night is long gone. The mud kept the truth and let the rest go.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. It never once lied to me. Even now it declines to start.
Nothing. It never had anything to say and it never pretended otherwise, and in this town that made it remarkable.
A drip off the boardwalk into it, slow, unbothered, in no hurry for anything.

overrides.PICK_UP: I took a little, in a twist of paper. The one honest thing in the territory. A man should keep a sample of what saved him.

subjects.name: THE HILLS
LOOK_AT: The hills, gone gold at the top — the ordinary kind, the kind the sun hands out free every morning and nobody ever had to dig for.
Gold country. For the first time since I arrived, that is simply a true statement.
The diggings are quiet, and the hills look, for once, like hills.
LISTEN_TO: Very faint, and for the first time since I stepped off the coach: no picks. The hills, being left alone.
Nothing. They are extremely large, and they are not doing anything, and there is gold in them.
The wind coming down off them, cool, carrying nothing at all. It is a relief to hear nothing in a place that used to be so loud about it.

overrides.TALK_TO: I told them they could rest now. Presumptuous, possibly. But somebody ought to say it, and the piano man had the morning free.
